intro.author: Much of the book is Nehemiah's own first-person memoir (1:1). It was joined with Ezra, and the two were counted as one book in the Hebrew Bible.
intro.written: Probably late in the 400s BC, not long after the events. Nehemiah arrived in Jerusalem in 445/444 BC, the twentieth year of Artaxerxes I.
intro.audience: The Jewish community in and around Jerusalem, and later generations learning from their example
intro.setting: About ninety years after the first exiles returned, Jerusalem's temple stood but its walls lay in ruins and the city was thinly populated. Judah was a small Persian province surrounded by hostile neighbors.
intro.purpose: To record how God used Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem's walls and, with Ezra, to renew the people's commitment to God's law.
intro.bigIdea: Prayer and hard work go together as God's people rebuild both their city and their faithfulness.

outline.title: The law read, sins confessed, covenant made
Jerusalem repopulated and the wall dedicated
